title: Editor ignores special keys when using alternative keyboard layout (Neo2, NeoQwertz)
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in v4.4.beta3.official [06acfccf8] and later (tested up to v4.5.beta3.official [4d1f26e1f]) - Non-reproducible in v4.4.beta2.official [a013481b0] and earlier (tested down to v3.6.1.stable.official [b1ba98fce]) ### System information Fedora Linux 42 (Workstation Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver - Gnome 48 ### Issue description I am using an alternative keyboard layout called NeoQwertz (https://www.neo-layout.org/Layouts/neoqwertz/) which adds additional layers to have more functions available close to the home row. The physical keyboard type is German ISO. Up to 4.4.beta2 this works just fine with Godot, but starting with 4.4.beta3 the special keys on layer 4 don't work anymore. When holding down a mod key the left half of the alpha keys become special keys like the arrow keys, backspace, delete, return, escape and tab (the right part basically becomes a numpad). See the following image on how the layout looks. Mod4 / M4 being the mod keys that activate the layer. The left half of layer 4 does not work anymore since 4.4.beta3. The right half of the same layer, containing mostly the number keys, however still works. Only non-printable chars / keys seem to be affected. At first I thought the mod keys were the problem, as I think both of them are specific to the ISO layout (the one to the right of shift simply does not exists in ANSI and the one to the right of space has a different keycode I assume), but that would not explain only the left half being affected. I have searched the issue tracker and found a number of issues related to keyboard layouts and physical keycodes vs "normal" keycodes but none quite fit and all of them were closed anyway. Though it made me suspect that the flexible, thus probably complicated, handling of shortcuts in Godot in relation to keycode vs physical location might be part of the problem. Maybe some fix introduced to handle other edge cases caused this? Looking for keyboard related merges between 4.4.beta2 and 4.4.beta3 is probably a good place to start. I want to stress that I have been using this layout for quite some time and I never had any problems with any desktop application. I assume that Godot is different because of the physical keycode functionality. Things I have already tested to narrow down the problem: - Tested the Colemak layout, which swaps capslock out for backspace. That works for all Godot versions I tested. The difference is that in this case the remapped key is on the first layer. Now thinking the problem only arises when a second key is held, I tried with NeoQwertz again but locked the layer 4 (by pressing both Mod4 keys at the same time the layer remains active until both of them are pressed again). It still did not work, so the second key being pressed at the same time does not seem to be the culprit. Maybe it has to do with the control keys being on a higher layer? - I used the key remapper kanata to remap the spacebar to backspace, which worked in all versions of Godot, supporting the previous point that just the remapping of a special key does not seem to be the main cause of the problem. - I tested with KDE in addition to Gnome, to rule out that the problem is Gnome specific (the application of the layout is done by the desktop environment). I do understand that this is a rather niche issue, but maybe someone familiar with the input system has an idea or can point me towards further tests to narrow down the issue. ### Steps to reproduce (I don't know if this is reproducible without an ISO keyboard. I don't know it the issue could theoretically be reproduced on Windows or Mac.) - change keyboard layout to NeoQwertz or Neo2 - both are the same on layer 3 and higher, but Neo2 also changes the alpha keys - both should be preinstalled on modern linux distributions - in Gnome only Neo2 is visible by default, to make NeoQwertz visible execute "gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.input-sources show-all-sources true" - layout names: German (Neo, QWERTZ) and German (Neo 2) - start Godot (4.4.beta3 or newer) and open any script file or editable text box - hold down one of the Mod4 keys ("Alt Gr" or "<", see picture of layout) and type for example: - F -> should behave like right arrow - V -> should behave like return - X -> should behave like tab - observe that nothing is happening ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
